T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou  following:
 ORDER 1 .

This appeal has been filed under Section 378(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for seeking leave to appeal against the judgment of acquittal dated 19.12.2017 passed by the JMFC,
District-Dhar Criminal Case No.2339/2011 whereby the accused have been acquitted from the offence under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) r/w (ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Hence, the The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Jitendra on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187515796/
1 present petition for grant of leave.
2 .

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant/state has submitted that the trial Court has wrongly appreciated the evidence and acquitted the respondents.

It is further contended that the seized packed water will came under definition of "food" as per the Gazette notification of Govt. of India dated 21.03.2001, but the learned trial Court has acquitted the respondents without considering the same.
Hence, the order of learned trial Court is not sustainable in the eyes of law.

3. On the other hand, counsel for the respondents opposed the prayer by submitting that the the pouch of water itself contains the date of expiry as one month i.e. on 20.06.2011, but the same were investigated in the laboratory on 21.07.2011 after the expiry of one month and one day.
Hence, the learned trial Court has rightly acquitted the respondents.
4. That apart, it is also submitted that as per the mandatory provisions of the Act, the company has not made party in the present case.
Hence, the prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. In view of the submissions advanced by counsel for the State, I have gone through the record and impugned judgment.

6. From the record, it is clear that the date of expiry of the water/packaging water pouches is mentioned as 20.06.2011, but the same were investigated in the laboratory on 21.07.2011 after the expiry of one month and one day, hence, in view of the aforesaid, the findings of learned trial Court warrant no interference.
That apart, the prosecution has also not complied with the provisions of Section 17 of the Act.
Hence, the findings are not suffering from any illegality or infirmity.
7 . In view of the aforesaid, the application of leave to appeal against acquittal is hereby rejected.
Resultantly, this appeal is hereby dismissed.
8. Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the trial Court concerned for information.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE amit The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Jitendra on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187515796/
